title: optimize CPU request path: reduce serialization overhead, improve thread-pool and core pinning
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: CPU-side request path was a measurable bottleneck for small/medium requests when model kernels were fast (e.g., quantized LMs). This PR targets three hotspots: (1) expensive JSON/binary serialization on the fast path, (2) contention and suboptimal scheduling in the global thread-pool, and (3) lack of consistent core pinning which caused cache-thrashing at high concurrency. Summary of changes: Move request/response serialization off the synchronous fast path into an async serializer queue with a preallocated buffer pool to reduce copies and transient allocations; introduce a two-tier thread pool with a small low-latency worker pool pinned to dedicated CPU cores for request dispatch and KV cache access and a larger background pool for serialization and telemetry; implement lightweight core pinning helpers and a platform abstraction that pins low-latency workers to a CPU affinity mask derived from instance topology; improve KV cache hot-path by replacing a single global lock with sharded reader-optimized hash maps and per-shard sequence counters to reduce writer-reader contention; add metrics for serialization queue length, per-pool busy-time, and per-core request counts and expose them in the runtime metrics endpoint. Benchmarks and results: Synthetic tracing harness: p50 request latency improved from 35ms -> 18ms (~49% reduction), p99 improved from 220ms -> 95ms (~57% reduction); end-to-end throughput with continuous batching increased ~1.6x at 95th percentile concurrency; CPU utilization per-request dropped ~40% on driver CPU threads under real workload. Testing and safety: Added unit tests for serializer and buffer pool, integration tests for graceful shutdown, a perf_canary stress test running 10k requests across 8 simulated clients, and a runtime flag cpu_optimize.request_path_v2 with safe fallback. Migration and rollout: Default rollout is opt-in via runtime flag with a 48-hour canary on dedicated pools before enabling by default; observability includes serialization-queue-latency and per-pool-saturation metrics. Checklist: [x] Implement async serializer and buffer pool; [x] Two-tier thread pool with affinity helpers; [x] Sharded KV cache updates; [x] Add metrics and expose via /metrics; [x] Unit & integration tests; [x] Benchmarks attached in PR comments. Related: ENG-4231, ENG-4278.
